data.name: Gateway Arch Visitor Center
data.description: The Gateway Arch Visitor Center, located directly under the Gateway Arch, is the central location for the journey to the top, the Arch Museum, the film Monument to the Dream, the Arch Store and the Arch cafe. Enter the Visitor Center from Smith Square to the west of the Arch directly across from the Old Courthouse. The North and South legs of the Gateway Arch are exit only from the visitor center and museum.
data.audioDescription: The Gateway Arch Visitor Center is a semicircular wall of glass and steel built into the berm directly below the soaring Gateway Arch. The glass catches the light and gleams. The entrance curves around a round pool that shows the reflection of the entrance and the Arch. Passing through the glass door to either side of the curve, the bright, white entrance area has the ticket center on the left, an information desk in the middle and the security area on the right. Once you pass through security, you descend an escalator into a large area with a soaring white ceiling passing by a mezzanine that has a terrazzo floor with an embedded map showing the path of many trails to the west from St. Louis. Descending further on the escalator you see large screens with movies of natural scenes and reenactments of explorers and pioneers. Passing through the middle of these large screens you enter the museum which features many touchable exhibits for guests with low vision.
data.passportStampLocationDescription: The Passport stamp is a circle with the name Gateway Arch National Park along the top, the date in the middle and St. Louis, MO along the bottom.

data.directionsInfo: Gateway Arch National Park is located in the heart of downtown St. Louis on the Mississippi River. Interstate Routes 44, 55, 64 and 70 converge near the park. The Gateway Arch is easily accessible from St. Louis' MetroLink Lightrail. Board at any station and exit at 8th and Pine or Lacledes Landing and follow the signs to the Memorial (a 10 min. walk) Please note: Visitors now enter the Arch through the west entrance, which faces Fourth Street and the Old Courthouse. The Gateway Arch legs are now exit only.

data.name: Old Courthouse
data.description: This historic building features modern exhibits on the United States court system and on Dred and Harriet Scott, who sued for their freedom from slavery in a courtroom there nearly 200 years ago.
